# Deployment

Keep provider keys, tools, and business logic on the server; connect user devices to your backend,
not straight to the provider. How audio travels between the device and the model depends on the
client and the provider:

- **[Browser WebRTC + server sideband](#browser-webrtc-server-sideband)** — the recommended browser
  path on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI: the browser exchanges media directly with the provider (lowest
  latency) while your backend runs the agent over a control-plane sideband.
- **[Browser → backend WebSocket relay](#browser-backend-websocket-relay)** — works with every
  provider, including Gemini Live, xAI, and ElevenLabs Agents: the browser streams audio to your backend, which owns the
  media bridge.
- **[SIP / telephony bridge](#siptelephony-bridge)** — for phone calls, via a telephony provider.

[Hosting the backend](#hosting) covers what the server running these sessions needs: long-lived
connections, routing, timeouts, and draining on deploy.

In every setup the session — with its [tools](tools.md), [history](history.md), and
[usage limits](observability.md#usage-and-limits) — runs on your backend. Wiring a browser straight
to the provider with the provider's own SDK instead moves the agent loop into the client and gives
up all of that; prefer one of the setups above.

## Browser WebRTC + server sideband {#browser-webrtc-server-sideband}

For browser voice agents on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, the browser carries microphone and speaker
audio directly over WebRTC while the backend attaches a control-plane **sideband** to the same call.
Media never touches your backend, so latency stays low, while tools, history, dependencies, and
provider credentials stay on the server. Gemini Live, xAI, and ElevenLabs Agents do not offer this sideband transport —
use the [WebSocket relay](#browser-backend-websocket-relay) there.

```text
browser ── WebRTC media ── provider
   │                         ▲
   └─ SDP offer → backend ───┘ sideband identified by call_id
```

Relay the browser's offer with
[`AgentRealtime.answer_webrtc_offer`][pydantic_ai.agent.AgentRealtime.answer_webrtc_offer], return
the SDP answer to the browser, then attach the returned call handle:

```python
import asyncio

from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a concise voice assistant.')
realtime = agent.realtime('{{ openai:realtime }}')
sideband_tasks: set[asyncio.Task[None]] = set()


async def handle_offer(sdp_offer: str) -> str:
    answer = await realtime.answer_webrtc_offer(sdp_offer)

    async def run_sideband() -> None:
        async with realtime.session(provider_session=answer.session) as session:
            async for event in session:
                print(event)

    task = asyncio.create_task(run_sideband())
    sideband_tasks.add(task)  # (1)!
    task.add_done_callback(sideband_tasks.discard)
    return answer.sdp
```

1. asyncio keeps only a weak reference to a task, so hold one yourself until the call ends; the done
   callback also surfaces an error the sideband session raised instead of leaving it as a "never
   retrieved" warning.

The secure offer-relay flow never gives the browser a token. As an alternative,
[`AgentRealtime.create_client_secret`][pydantic_ai.agent.AgentRealtime.create_client_secret] mints a
short-lived credential for client-led negotiation: the browser posts its offer to the secret's
[`webrtc_url`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeClientSecret.webrtc_url] with the secret as its
bearer token. Either way the browser is a peer on the provider
session and can send provider-native control events, so authorize every server-side tool against
trusted [`deps`](../dependencies.md), not session instructions supplied to the model.

To continue an earlier conversation, create the `AgentRealtime` per call inside the offer handler,
`realtime = agent.realtime(model, message_history=...)`, and answer the offer and open the sideband from
that same object. GPT-Live takes the history when the offer starts the call, and a sideband opened with
other history refuses to attach; the other providers seed it when the sideband attaches.

!!! warning "The browser can read seeded history"
    Seeding a WebRTC call with [`message_history`](history.md) sends those prior turns into the
    **shared** provider conversation that the browser is a peer on, so a call participant can read
    them — including confidential tool results — over the data channel (Azure's `webrtcfilter=on`
    still forwards conversation-item events). Only seed a call with history that is safe for the
    browser to see; keep confidential context in [`deps`](../dependencies.md) and tool logic instead.

A sideband does not own the audio transport: its `send_audio()`, `commit_audio()`, `clear_audio()`,
and `stream_audio()` methods raise, and `audio_retention` must remain `'transcript_only'`. Enable
[input transcription](audio.md#input-transcription) when user speech must appear in history. On
gpt-realtime and Azure OpenAI, use
[`RealtimeOutputSpeechStartEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeOutputSpeechStartEvent] /
[`RealtimeOutputSpeechEndEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeOutputSpeechEndEvent] for speaking
indicators, and [`interrupt()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.interrupt] clears the provider's
outbound WebRTC audio buffer so [barge-in](turns.md#barge-in) stops playback. GPT-Live emits neither
event and doesn't support `interrupt()` (see
[its feature support](openai.md#gpt-live-feature-support-and-limitations)). A dropped sideband
follows the same [reconnect](lifecycle.md#reconnecting) rules, with one wrinkle covered there: a
clean close is treated as the browser hanging up.

Closing a sideband session, or leaving its `async with` block, only detaches your server: the
browser's call stays up, and billed, until the browser hangs up. To end the call from the server,
call [`hang_up()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.hang_up] instead (it works from a
[tool](tools.md#ending-the-session-from-a-tool) too), or
[`hang_up(answer.session)`][pydantic_ai.agent.AgentRealtime.hang_up] on `agent.realtime(model)` when
no sideband is attached. OpenAI supports this for both gpt-realtime and GPT-Live, and so does Azure OpenAI.

The [realtime WebRTC example](../examples/realtime-webrtc.md) demonstrates the full FastAPI and
browser flow. Provider-specific setup (Azure's Microsoft Entra ID and `webrtcfilter`) lives on the
[Azure](azure.md#browser-webrtc-and-microsoft-entra-id) page.

## Browser → backend WebSocket relay {#browser-backend-websocket-relay}

When the browser can't use WebRTC — or the provider is Gemini Live, xAI, or ElevenLabs Agents — build a WebSocket
endpoint on your backend that accepts the browser's microphone audio and pumps it into
[`send_audio()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.send_audio], while relaying
[`stream_audio()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.stream_audio] output back for playback. Here
the backend owns the media bridge. The [realtime camera example](../examples/realtime-camera.md)
demonstrates this setup end to end; a minimal FastAPI relay — the browser sends raw PCM16 binary
frames and plays the frames it receives — is:

```python
import asyncio

from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket

from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a helpful voice assistant.')
app = FastAPI()


@app.websocket('/voice')
async def voice_socket(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()

    async def microphone():
        while True:
            yield await websocket.receive_bytes()

    async with agent.realtime('{{ openai:realtime }}').session() as session:

        async def playback():
            async for chunk in session.stream_audio():
                await websocket.send_bytes(chunk)

        playback_task = asyncio.create_task(playback())
        try:
            await session.send_audio(microphone())
        finally:
            playback_task.cancel()
```

[`send_audio()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.send_audio] consumes the async iterator for the
whole call, so when the browser disconnects, `receive_bytes()` raises, the `finally` stops playback,
and leaving the `async with` block hangs up the provider session. Driving the input from a bare
`asyncio.create_task` instead would swallow that error and leave the billed session open with nobody
listening.

`handle_barge_in=True` is a no-op for this relay: `played_audio_bytes` counts a chunk as played when
the relay forwards it, before the browser has actually played it, so the session sees no unplayed
audio to flush. The relay must obtain the browser's real playback position, call
[`interrupt(played_bytes=...)`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.interrupt] with that count, and
tell the browser to stop playback and clear its own buffer: the session can only drop what it has
not forwarded yet. Passing `played_ms=` records the provider-side cutoff but never flushes audio
queued by the session or buffered in the browser.

## SIP/telephony bridge

Terminate the phone call with a telephony provider such as Twilio, then build the service that
connects its media stream (e.g. Twilio Media Streams over WebSocket) to the backend session,
transcoding between the line's codec and PCM16.

## Hosting the backend {#hosting}

A realtime session is not a request. It is a task that holds a WebSocket to the provider open for the
whole call (on a [WebRTC sideband](#browser-webrtc-server-sideband), the control-plane WebSocket),
next to the client's own connection in the [relay](#browser-backend-websocket-relay) and telephony
setups. Each [`session()`][pydantic_ai.agent.AgentRealtime.session] opens its own provider connection,
and one process can run many sessions on its event loop. Unlike a
[standard agent](../production.md#deploy), where any instance can continue any conversation, a call
lives in the process that holds it: its provider connection, running tools, and (on Gemini) resumption
handles, which [can't be moved to another process](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues/7302).

A WebSocket stays on the instance that accepted it, so the relay needs no extra routing; if your app
splits one call across several requests, route them to the instance holding the session. A client that
reconnects elsewhere gets a new provider session; to carry the conversation over, store
[`all_messages()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.all_messages] and
[seed](history.md#seeding-a-session) the new session with it.

In the relay and telephony setups, where the client's connection is the request, set the platform's
request or connection timeout above your longest call. Providers cap a connection's
duration too, and a `reconnect` policy survives that cap on most of them (see
[provider session limits](lifecycle.md#provider-session-limits)), but nothing recovers the client's
connection when your platform cuts it: in the relay above, the browser socket closing ends the session.
Enforce your own maximum call length with a [watchdog](lifecycle.md#ending-a-call) instead, ending a
sideband call as described below.

Scale on concurrent calls rather than request rate; a relay also carries every call's audio through
the backend, so watch its bandwidth and CPU. A deploy has to drain: stop sending new calls to an
instance and let its sessions finish before it exits, which can take far longer than the few seconds of
shutdown grace many platforms give by default. To end calls sooner, end them deliberately; on a
sideband that means [`hang_up()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.hang_up], because a sideband
whose process exits without hanging up leaves the browser's call up, and billed, with no agent behind
it (see [the sideband section](#browser-webrtc-server-sideband) and
[Ending a call](lifecycle.md#ending-a-call)).

Long-running compute fits this directly: containers or VMs behind a load balancer that supports
WebSockets. Platforms that cap requests work within their limits: Cloud Run, for example, counts a
relay's WebSocket against its request timeout, which can be raised to an hour, so a longer call has to
continue on a new connection and session. Request-scoped functions don't fit. With AWS Lambda behind
an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API, API Gateway holds the client's connection but invokes the function
once per message, so no invocation lives long enough to hold the provider connection between messages.
The session has to run on long-lived compute instead. API Gateway can still front it, but then you
build the routing yourself: a registry that sends each message to the instance holding that call's
session, audio base64-encoded in text frames (it rejects binary ones) and sent back through its
`@connections` API, and a connection that closes after ten idle minutes or two hours.

[Browser WebRTC](#browser-webrtc-server-sideband) takes media off your servers: audio flows directly
between the browser and the provider, and your backend carries only the sideband. But in the
[offer handler above](#browser-webrtc-server-sideband), the sideband runs as a background task after
the handler has returned the SDP answer, so no request or connection stays open for the call and the
platform can't see it. Give the sideband CPU outside requests (on Cloud Run, instance-based rather than
the default request-based billing) or run it on a worker or VM; scale on your own count of live
sideband tasks, since request metrics show an idle instance; and on shutdown, wait for the tasks in
`sideband_tasks` or hang up their calls before the process exits.

# ElevenLabs

Pydantic AI connects to [ElevenLabs](https://elevenlabs.io) in two ways:

- [ElevenLabs Agents](#elevenlabs-agents) runs the conversation on an agent hosted and configured on
  [ElevenAgents](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/overview), ElevenLabs' agent platform (its voice, LLM,
  knowledge base, and tools), which Pydantic AI takes over per conversation.
- [Eleven Realtime](#eleven-realtime) runs ElevenLabs' speech-to-speech models directly, with the instructions,
  tools, and history coming from your Pydantic AI agent, as with every other
  [realtime provider](overview.md#provider-support).

The difference is where the agent is defined. Use Eleven Realtime unless you need the ElevenAgents platform: your
Pydantic AI agent defines the conversation, as it does with any other realtime provider, and a reconnect replays
the history.

Use ElevenLabs Agents when the agent lives on the ElevenAgents platform, for its knowledge bases, workflows, and
guardrails, or to run a cascaded pipeline with an LLM of your choice. Pydantic AI then overrides the agent's
instructions and settings per conversation, and by default checks its client tools against your agent's tools
(or [syncs them](#tool-synchronization) to match; see [Configuration ownership](#configuration-ownership)). An
ElevenAgents agent can also run on an Eleven Realtime model, in [Realtime voice mode](#configuration-ownership):
that's configured on the agent, and you connect to it through ElevenLabs Agents.

## ElevenLabs Agents

Use an `elevenlabs-agents:<agent_id>` model string, or
[`ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel`][pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents.ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel] for
model-level configuration, to connect an agent to the
[ElevenAgents](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/overview) platform, where the conversation runs on a
hosted agent. Start with the [realtime quickstart](overview.md#quickstart).

ElevenLabs Agents runs a cascaded pipeline (realtime ASR, a configurable LLM, ElevenLabs TTS, and
a server-side turn-taking model) behind a pre-provisioned agent, which the conversation reaches
over the agent WebSocket. The model wraps that *hosted agent*, addressed by its `agent_id`, and
Pydantic AI takes ownership of as much of the conversation as ElevenLabs allows per conversation
(see [Configuration ownership](#configuration-ownership)).

### Setup

To use ElevenLabs Agents, install `pydantic-ai-slim` with the `elevenlabs-agents-realtime` optional group,
which bundles the realtime WebSocket transport:

```bash
pip/uv-add "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-agents-realtime]"
```

Set `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, or pass an
[`ElevenLabsProvider`][pydantic_ai.providers.elevenlabs.ElevenLabsProvider] with `api_key=`. The
key is required even for public agents, because the connect-time preflight authenticates with it.
The provider's `base_url` doubles as the region switch: pass a
[data-residency host](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/product-guides/administration/data-residency) such
as `https://api.eu.residency.elevenlabs.io` (or the India and Singapore hosts,
`api.in.residency.elevenlabs.io` and `api.sg.residency.elevenlabs.io`) to keep both the REST calls and the
WebSocket inside a region.

Connecting starts with a REST preflight that fetches the agent: a bad key or an unknown agent id raises a
[`ModelHTTPError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelHTTPError] from it, and an API that can't be reached raises a
[`RealtimeError`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeError]. With `elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync` set to `'error'` (the
default) or `'off'`, the key only reads; `'sync'` also needs write access to agents and tools.

### Before you connect

1. Create the agent in the [ElevenLabs dashboard](https://elevenlabs.io/app/agents) or through the ElevenLabs API,
   and copy its id.
2. Under *Security* > *Overrides* in the agent's settings, turn on *System prompt* if the Pydantic AI agent has
   instructions or a system prompt, plus the toggle of each override setting you use (see [Settings](#settings)).
3. Under *Advanced* > *Client events*, add `context_usage`, which reports context usage and marks where a spoken
   response ends (see [Usage and cost](#usage-and-cost)).
4. Pick a [tool synchronization](#tool-synchronization) mode: with the default, `'error'`, a difference between the
   session's tools and the agent's client tools fails the connect.

This agent keeps the ElevenLabs agent's client tools in sync with its own:

```python {title="elevenlabs_agents_tools.py"}
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents import ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a friendly concierge. Keep answers short.')


@agent.tool_plain
async def find_restaurant(cuisine: str, party_size: int) -> str:
    """Find a restaurant with a free table.

    Args:
        cuisine: The kind of food the guests want, e.g. 'Italian'.
        party_size: How many guests need a seat.
    """
    return f'Trattoria Roma has a table for {party_size} ({cuisine}).'


realtime_agent = agent.realtime(
    'elevenlabs-agents:agent_0101k2example',
    model_settings=ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings(elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync='sync'),
)
```

ElevenLabs needs a description for every tool parameter, which the `Args:` section of the docstring provides.

### Model names

Use `elevenlabs-agents:<agent_id>` as a model string, for example `elevenlabs-agents:agent_0101k2...`, or pass the
agent id, `agent_0101k2...`, to `ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel`. The agent's own configuration decides the ASR setup, audio formats, turn-taking, and
which per-conversation overrides are permitted. Every
[`ModelResponse`][pydantic_ai.messages.ModelResponse] is stamped with the agent id as its
`model_name`; the LLM the agent runs on is part of the agent configuration and is not reported per
response.

That LLM doesn't always answer. When it errors, returns nothing or an invalid tool call, or goes quiet for longer
than the agent's `prompt.cascade_timeout_seconds` (4 seconds by default; in [Realtime voice mode](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/realtime-models), ElevenLabs sets this wait itself), ElevenLabs answers the turn with a backup
LLM from its fallback cascade. The response's `model_name` is still the agent id: only a `context_usage` report
(see [Usage and cost](#usage-and-cost)) names the LLM, and it isn't tied to a response. The conversations API reports
the answering LLM afterwards, per message, as `producing_llm`. To turn the cascade off, set the agent's `prompt.backup_llm_config` to `{"preference": "disabled"}`.
To choose the backup LLMs, set it to `{"preference": "override", "order": [...]}`.

### Configuration ownership

Pydantic AI is the source of truth wherever ElevenLabs allows a per-conversation override, and
fails loudly where it does not:

- **Instructions**: when the Pydantic AI agent defines instructions or a system prompt, the ElevenLabs agent must
  permit the *System prompt* override; otherwise the preflight raises a
  [`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError] naming the exact toggle. Without local
  instructions, the ElevenLabs-side prompt is inherited silently.
- **Overrides**: first message, language, voice, TTS knobs, the pipeline LLM, and text-only mode
  are sent in the conversation-initiation override payload. Every override is gated by a per-field
  toggle under *Security* > *Overrides* in the agent's settings
  (`platform_settings.overrides` via the API); the preflight checks each override setting against
  the agent's allowlist before dialing. The raw `elevenlabs_agents_config_override` escape hatch is the one
  exception; see [Settings](#settings).
- **Tools**: client tools are workspace entities referenced by the agent, so they cannot be
  declared inline per conversation. By default the preflight errors when the session's tools and
  the agent's client tools differ in any way; see [Tool synchronization](#tool-synchronization).
- **Stays with the agent**: turn-taking and VAD, ASR configuration, audio formats, the voice mode, and platform
  settings (auth, privacy, guardrails, knowledge bases, workflows).
- **Realtime voice mode**: an agent set to a
  [Realtime model](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/realtime-models) (its
  `conversation_config.realtime_model`, which can't be overridden per conversation) has ElevenLabs pick the LLM and
  TTS model. It would ignore `elevenlabs_agents_llm` and an `elevenlabs_agents_tts` `model_id`, so the preflight
  raises a [`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError] for either. Every other override works as in Custom mode.

### Settings

[`ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings`][pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents.ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings] —
the realtime counterpart of [model run settings](../agent.md#model-run-settings) — extends the
[shared settings](overview.md#shared-settings) with the agent's per-conversation overrides
(greeting, language, voice, TTS delivery, the pipeline LLM), dynamic variables, and the tool
synchronization mode:

```python
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents import (
    ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel,
    ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings,
)

settings = ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings(
    elevenlabs_agents_voice_id='EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL',
    elevenlabs_agents_language='de',
    elevenlabs_agents_first_message='Hallo! Wie kann ich helfen?',
    elevenlabs_agents_tts={'stability': 0.4, 'speed': 1.05},
)
model = ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel('agent_0101k2example', settings=settings)
```

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `elevenlabs_agents_first_message`, `elevenlabs_agents_language` | The greeting the agent opens with and the conversation language |
| `elevenlabs_agents_voice_id`, `elevenlabs_agents_tts` | The provider voice and the TTS delivery knobs (model, stability, speed, similarity boost) |
| `elevenlabs_agents_llm` | The LLM the ElevenLabs pipeline runs, by its ElevenLabs model id |
| `elevenlabs_agents_dynamic_variables` | Values substituted into `{{placeholders}}` in the agent's prompts and messages |
| `elevenlabs_agents_custom_llm_extra_body` | Extra request body for an agent backed by a custom LLM; gated by its own security toggle |
| `elevenlabs_agents_user_id` | Opaque end-user identifier for ElevenLabs-side analytics |
| `elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags` | Whether expressive audio tags such as `[laughs]` are removed from the agent's transcripts (`True` by default); see [Provider-specific quirks](#provider-specific-quirks) |
| `elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync` | How the session's tools are reconciled with the agent's client tools; see [Tool synchronization](#tool-synchronization) |
| `elevenlabs_agents_config_override` | Raw override keys merged last as a forward-compatibility escape hatch |

Each `elevenlabs_agents_*` override setting requires its toggle on the agent, as described above;
`elevenlabs_agents_dynamic_variables`, `elevenlabs_agents_user_id`, `elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags`, and
`elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync` need none.
`elevenlabs_agents_config_override` is the one setting deliberately not checked against the permission
allowlist — being raw is its point — so a field the agent does not permit there surfaces as the
server closing the socket (code 1008, naming the field) after the handshake, not as a local
[`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError].

Of the shared settings:

- `output_modality='text'` maps to the text-only override, toggle-gated like the rest.
- `tool_choice='none'` and [`ToolOrOutput`][pydantic_ai.settings.ToolOrOutput] allow-lists restrict
  the conversation to those tools through the agent's *Tool IDs* override, toggle-gated like the
  rest: the agent keeps every tool of the run attached, and the conversation leaves the others out.
  A choice that forces a tool call (`'required'`, or a list of tool names) raises, as on the other
  providers.
- `turn_detection=False` raises: ElevenLabs' server-side turn model is always on, so there is no
  [push-to-talk](turns.md#push-to-talk). The [`TurnDetection`][pydantic_ai.realtime.TurnDetection] knobs
  are ignored; tune turn-taking on the agent's `conversation_config.turn` instead.
- `input_transcription_model` is ignored: ASR drives the agent pipeline, so input is always transcribed,
  even with `None`.
- `reconnect` is ignored with an
  [`UnsupportedSettingWarning`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnsupportedSettingWarning]: a conversation can't be
  resumed, so a dropped connection ends the session rather than starting one that remembers nothing.
- `max_tokens`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `async_tool_calls`, and `thinking` have no per-conversation
  surface and are ignored, matching the [shared settings contract](overview.md#shared-settings);
  `parallel_tool_calls=False` warns with an
  [`UnsupportedSettingWarning`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnsupportedSettingWarning].

### Audio formats

Audio formats are fixed per agent, not per conversation. The model profile defaults to ElevenLabs'
16 kHz PCM defaults; the connect handshake echoes the agent's actual formats, and the model raises a
[`RealtimeError`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeError] when they disagree with the profile. For an
agent configured differently (e.g. 24 kHz), pass the actual rates via `profile=`:

```python
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents import ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel

model = ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel(
    'agent_0101k2example',
    profile={'audio_input_sample_rate': 24000, 'audio_output_sample_rate': 24000},
)
```

Telephony (`ulaw_8000`) agents are not supported.

### Tool synchronization

`elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync` controls how the session's
[`ToolDefinition`][pydantic_ai.tools.ToolDefinition]s are reconciled with the agent's client tools
at connect time:

- `'error'` (default): raise a [`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError] describing every
  difference (missing, extra, or differing tools), so the two can never silently disagree.
- `'sync'`: make the workspace match Pydantic AI over REST before dialing: create missing client
  tools, update differing ones, and re-point the agent's `tool_ids`, which detaches client tools the run
  doesn't define (server-side webhook, MCP, and system tools stay attached). A differing tool that another
  agent also uses isn't changed under it: this agent gets a copy of its own. This mutates workspace
  state shared by every conversation with the agent, which is why it is opt-in. Treat it as a
  deploy-time step — a warm-up connect after a tool change — rather than something a customer's
  first call should pay for: the writes run one after another, and two processes syncing the same
  agent concurrently race on the final `tool_ids` re-point, last writer wins. Synced tools get
  ElevenLabs' default 20-second response timeout (`response_timeout_secs`); a tool that already has a
  timeout of its own keeps it when it is updated.
- `'off'`: trust the agent's own tool definitions, e.g. for client tools set up on the ElevenLabs side
  with settings Pydantic AI doesn't sync. A call to a tool the session does not define reaches the tool
  manager like any other call and is answered with the standard unknown-tool error, which lands in the
  session's history.

Server-side webhook, MCP, and system tools on the agent are ElevenLabs-owned and never touched, and
ElevenLabs runs them itself. Its calls to webhook and system tools (such as `end_call`) aren't recorded in the
session's history; its calls to MCP tools are recorded as a
[`NativeToolCallPart`][pydantic_ai.messages.NativeToolCallPart] and
[`NativeToolReturnPart`][pydantic_ai.messages.NativeToolReturnPart]. MCP tools that require approval on
the ElevenLabs side aren't supported. The session denies such a call (with a warning) rather than leave
the conversation waiting up to 300 seconds for an approval that can't come. The agent's LLM is told that the user
denied the call, and ElevenLabs reports nothing further about it. Give the agent those tools through a Pydantic AI
[MCP toolset](../mcp/client.md) instead, which is the recommended way, or turn approval off for the tool
in the agent's configuration.

ElevenLabs stores tool parameters in its own restricted schema dialect rather than JSON Schema.
`type`, `description`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, and `required` are supported; other keywords
(such as `additionalProperties` or numeric bounds) are not; and **every parameter needs a
description**. Nested models (`$defs`/`$ref`) are inlined, and optional (nullable) parameters are
collapsed onto their non-null type before conversion, with optionality carried by `required` alone.
The dialect has no way to say `null` — a required nullable parameter is advertised as its
non-null type, and the agent's LLM, which only ever sees the advertised schema, always supplies a
value for it. `'sync'` therefore fails loudly for a tool whose parameters lack descriptions (add
them in the function docstring, and set
[`require_parameter_descriptions=True`](../tools.md#function-tools-and-schema) to catch a missing one when the
tool is defined) or use a shape the dialect cannot express (a union of types, or a
recursive reference). The `'error'` comparison checks what the dialect can express, comparing a
parameter's description only when the local schema declares one.

### Feature support and limitations

| Feature | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audio format | Full feature support | Mono PCM16; rates are fixed per agent (16 kHz default) and validated at connect, see [Audio formats](#audio-formats) |
| Text output | Limited parameter support | `output_modality='text'` maps to the text-only override, which needs its toggle on the agent |
| Image input | Unsupported | [`send()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.send] rejects images with a `UserError` |
| Manual turns | Unsupported | ElevenLabs' server-side turn model owns turn-taking; `turn_detection=False` raises |
| Explicit interruption/truncation | Unsupported | ElevenLabs [interrupts server-side](turns.md#barge-in) and emits `RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent`; `interrupt()` raises |
| Session seeding | Unsupported | The conversation WebSocket has no history-seeding channel |
| Input transcription | Full feature support | Always on: per-utterance final transcripts from the agent's ASR; `input_transcription_model` is ignored |
| Native tools | Unsupported | None can be configured from the session; configure [local fallbacks](tools.md#native-tools) for web capabilities. The agent's own MCP tool calls are recorded as `NativeToolCallPart`s named `mcp_server:<server id>` |
| Async tool calls | Unsupported | The agent waits for each tool result (see [concurrent tool execution](tools.md#concurrent-tool-execution)) |
| Usage | Limited parameter support | Context tokens only, with `context_usage` in the agent's `client_events`; no cost (see [Usage and cost](#usage-and-cost)) |
| Context window | Limited parameter support | Known only once the agent reports `context_usage`: `session.context_window_used` then gives the share of the LLM's context in use (see [Usage and cost](#usage-and-cost)) |
| Session duration | Limited parameter support | Capped by the agent's [maximum conversation duration](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/conversation-flow) (600 s by default, up to 7,200 s, set on the agent, not per conversation); at the cap the session gets a non-recoverable `RealtimeSessionErrorEvent` and raises a [`RealtimeError`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeError] |
| State-restoring reconnect | Unsupported | A dropped connection ends the session, and `reconnect` is ignored with a warning, see [Provider session limits](lifecycle.md#provider-session-limits) |

See [Audio, images, and transcripts](audio.md), [Turns and interruptions](turns.md),
[Tools](tools.md), and [Connection lifecycle](lifecycle.md) for the provider-agnostic workflows.

### Gateway

ElevenLabs is not currently available through the [Pydantic AI Gateway](../gateway.md). Connect
with an `elevenlabs-agents:<agent_id>` model string, or with `provider='elevenlabs'` or an
`ElevenLabsProvider`.

### Usage and cost

ElevenLabs reports the LLM's context consumption only, as `input_tokens`, and only when
`context_usage` is in the agent's `conversation.client_events` list (it is not by default, and adding it
is recommended: it also tells the session where a spoken response ends, see
[Provider-specific quirks](#provider-specific-quirks); a session on an agent without it warns once). A report arrives when the agent has finished generating a
response, with its last audio chunk (well before that audio has played), and counts toward the session's usage without belonging to any one response. When ElevenLabs
answers a turn with a fallback LLM, the report names that model and its context window. The context window it names is kept on
[`ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection.context_limit_tokens`][pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents.ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection.context_limit_tokens],
and [`context_window_used`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.context_window_used] is the ratio of
the two.

No price is known for the platform, so [`usage.cost`][pydantic_ai.usage.RunUsage.cost] is always
`None` and a [`cost_limit`][pydantic_ai.usage.UsageLimits.cost_limit] can't be enforced. Look the
cost up afterwards through the ElevenLabs conversations API: `GET /v1/convai/conversations/{conversation_id}`
reports the conversation's cost in credits as `metadata.cost`, its length as `metadata.call_duration_secs`, and a
breakdown, including the LLM tokens used per model, under `metadata.charging`. Every
[`ModelResponse`][pydantic_ai.messages.ModelResponse] the conversation ends, cut off and lost ones included,
carries the conversation's id in `provider_details['conversation_id']` (one still under way when the session
itself closes has none), and the live connection has it as
[`ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection.conversation_id`][pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents.ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection.conversation_id].

### Provider-specific quirks

- In audio mode, a response's transcript arrives whole once the agent's LLM has finished, which can be
  before or during its audio; only text-only mode streams it. Synthesis outruns playback, so a spoken
  response is usually delivered in full while the user is still hearing its first words.
- With a TTS model that voices expressive audio tags, such as `eleven_v3_conversational` or `eleven_v4_turbo`,
  the agent's LLM writes tags like `[laughs]` into its reply to direct the delivery, and ElevenLabs sends them as
  part of the response's transcript. Pydantic AI removes them, from the streamed transcript and the one in history
  alike, and keeps them, in order and without brackets, in the response's `provider_details['audio_tags']`
  (`['laughs']`). Only lowercase words in square brackets count as tags, so citations (`[1]`), Markdown links,
  and placeholders like `[Your Name]` stay in the text. Set `elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags=False` to keep the
  transcript as ElevenLabs sends it (`[laughs] Hi there.`). To keep the LLM from writing tags in the first place,
  turn off expressive mode on the agent (`tts.expressive_mode: false`), which also gives up the expressive delivery.
  This works only in Custom voice mode: in [Realtime voice mode](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/realtime-models), ElevenLabs manages expressive mode itself.
- A barge-in cuts each agent message down to what the user heard, as ElevenLabs reports it. Synthesis
  outruns playback, so this is usually after the message's response has ended. History then holds an
  [interrupted copy](history.md#transcription-and-history-edge-cases) of the response, in the same position,
  whose speech part has the heard text as its transcript: the cut-off message ends in `...`, and a message
  the user heard none of (one after it in the same turn) has no transcript. What the agent said is kept in
  the part's `provider_details['original_transcript']`. A response cut off while it is still being
  generated also carries the heard text in `provider_details['corrected_agent_response']`.
- A text turn goes out under an `id` naming it, and each reply says which text turns it answers (its
  `in_response_to_ids`), so [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] waits for
  the reply that answers the text: the one under way, if it names the text, and otherwise the next one. A reply
  that names a text also answers any text sent before it, as the agent folds text sent while it speaks into one
  reply, which can name only the latest. (Text sent while the agent speaks usually cuts it off, and the next reply
  answers it.)
- [`send(text, respond=False)`](turns.md#text-turns) is a `contextual_update`: the agent reads it from
  its next turn on, without stopping or replying. So is a [system prompt](turns.md#system-prompts) sent with
  `respond=False`, `<system>`-tagged.
- A response's parallel tool calls each run as soon as they arrive.
- With `elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync='off'`, client tools registered on the ElevenLabs side with
  `expects_response: false` are fire-and-forget: the session still runs them, but their results are never sent
  back to the agent. (The other modes require every client tool to expect a response.)
- A conversation waiting in the workspace's concurrency queue hears ElevenLabs' hold audio, which
  isn't part of the conversation; one that times out there ends with a
  [`RealtimeError`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeError] saying so.

## Eleven Realtime

Use an `elevenlabs:<model>` model string, or
[`ElevenLabsRealtimeModel`][pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs.ElevenLabsRealtimeModel] for model-level
configuration, to talk to ElevenLabs' [Eleven Realtime](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/realtime-models)
speech-to-speech models. Unlike [ElevenLabs Agents](#elevenlabs-agents), there is no hosted agent to configure:
the session speaks [ElevenLabs' OpenAI Realtime-compatible API](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/guides/openai-realtime-compatibility),
and Pydantic AI configures it from your agent. Start with the [realtime quickstart](overview.md#quickstart).

### Setup

To use Eleven Realtime, install `pydantic-ai-slim` with the `elevenlabs-realtime` optional group. It includes
the `openai` package, because the API reuses the OpenAI Realtime protocol's event types:

```bash
pip/uv-add "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-realtime]"
```

Set `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, or pass an
[`ElevenLabsProvider`][pydantic_ai.providers.elevenlabs.ElevenLabsProvider] with `api_key=`. The same key
and provider serve [ElevenLabs Agents](#elevenlabs-agents). To keep the connection in a
[data-residency region](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/data-residency), pass the region's
host as `base_url=`:

```python
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.providers.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsProvider
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsRealtimeModel

model = ElevenLabsRealtimeModel(
    '{{ elevenlabs:realtime.name }}',
    provider=ElevenLabsProvider(base_url='https://api.eu.residency.elevenlabs.io'),
)
agent = Agent(instructions='You are a friendly voice assistant.')
```

### Model names

Use the `elevenlabs:` prefix with a model name, e.g. `agent.realtime('{{ elevenlabs:realtime }}')`:

| Model | Optimized for |
| --- | --- |
| `eleven_realtime_v1_mini` | Price and latency |
| `eleven_realtime_v1_max` | Quality: it reasons before it responds, for complex instructions and multi-step tool use |

`eleven_realtime_v1_max` needs a [`max_tokens`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeModelSettings.max_tokens] of at
least 1024 (or none), isn't available in the India and Singapore data-residency regions, and costs more per
token. See [ElevenLabs' model list](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/realtime-models) for
the details.

### Settings

[`ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings`][pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs.ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings]
extends the [shared settings](overview.md#shared-settings):

```python
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsRealtimeModel, ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings

settings = ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings(
    elevenlabs_voice='george',
    elevenlabs_language='en',
    elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds=1800,
    turn_detection={'sensitivity': 'high'},
)
model = ElevenLabsRealtimeModel('{{ elevenlabs:realtime.name }}', settings=settings)
```

- `elevenlabs_voice` takes an ElevenLabs voice ID (e.g. `'JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb'`) or a default voice's name;
  the server's default is `'brian'`.
- `elevenlabs_language` sets the conversation's language (e.g. `'es'` or `'pt-br'`), which ElevenLabs uses for
  transcription, speech, and the model's replies. It defaults to English.
- `elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds` caps the session's length, from 60 to 7,200 seconds; see
  [Session length](#session-length).
- `elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags` (default `True`) removes expressive audio tags such as `[cheerful]` from the
  model's transcripts, as for ElevenLabs Agents; see
  [Provider-specific quirks](#eleven-realtime-quirks).

Turn detection is ElevenLabs' semantic VAD, which decides from what the user said, not only from silence,
whether they're done. The shared [`turn_detection`](turns.md#automatic-turn-detection) setting maps onto it:
`sensitivity` becomes its `eagerness` (`'low'`, `'medium'`, or `'high'`), and `prefix_padding_ms` and
`silence_duration_ms` are passed through. `turn_detection=False` turns it off for
[push-to-talk](turns.md#push-to-talk).

The session is configured through the OpenAI Realtime protocol, so `ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings` also takes
the [`OpenAIRealtimeModelSettings`][pydantic_ai.realtime.openai.OpenAIRealtimeModelSettings] fields.
`openai_turn_detection` takes a [`SemanticVAD`][pydantic_ai.realtime.openai.SemanticVAD], which sets
`create_response` and `interrupt_response` too; a [`ServerVAD`][pydantic_ai.realtime.openai.ServerVAD] raises
a `UserError`, as ElevenLabs only supports semantic VAD. ElevenLabs accepts and then ignores the other
OpenAI fields, so Pydantic AI doesn't send them: `openai_voice` (use `elevenlabs_voice`),
`openai_input_noise_reduction`, `openai_output_speed`, `openai_truncation`, and `openai_prune_tool_items`.
Of the shared settings, `parallel_tool_calls` and `thinking` are ignored the same way, and
`parallel_tool_calls=False` warns with an
[`UnsupportedSettingWarning`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnsupportedSettingWarning], as on a standard model.

[Input transcription](audio.md#input-transcription) is always on: each spoken turn's transcript arrives whole
once the turn is committed, usually after the reply has started. It takes no model, so
`input_transcription_model` is ignored: `None` still leaves transcripts on, and a pinned model ID has no effect.

### Feature support and limitations

| Feature | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audio format | Limited parameter support | Mono PCM16 at 24 kHz, input and output. The input rate is configurable (set `audio_input_sample_rate` through [`profile=`](overview.md#provider-support)); output is always 24 kHz. The API also offers G.711, which Pydantic AI does not expose |
| Text output | Unsupported | ElevenLabs answers text input in text, but then ignores audio input altogether, so `output_modality='text'` raises a `UserError` |
| Image input | Unsupported | ElevenLabs drops images from the conversation, so [`send()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.send] rejects them with a `UserError` before sending |
| Manual turns | Full feature support | `turn_detection=False` plus [commit/create verbs](turns.md#push-to-talk) |
| Interruption | Full feature support | [`interrupt()`](turns.md#barge-in) cancels the response, and `played_ms` truncates what the model remembers saying to what the user heard |
| Session seeding | Limited parameter support | User and assistant text only; seeded audio and images are unsupported |
| Input transcription | Limited parameter support | Always on, with whole-turn transcripts; no transcription model to choose |
| Native tools | Unsupported | ElevenLabs offers MCP tools, which Pydantic AI does not expose yet |
| Async tool calls | Unsupported | The model answers the user while a [tool runs](tools.md#concurrent-tool-execution), but then abandons the call, see [Provider-specific quirks](#eleven-realtime-quirks) |
| Usage | Unsupported | ElevenLabs reports no usage, so token counts are zero and `usage.cost` is `None` |
| Reconnection | Full feature support | Pydantic AI [replays completed local history](lifecycle.md#state-restoration) into a new session; in-flight media is lost |

See [Audio, images, and transcripts](audio.md), [Turns and interruptions](turns.md),
[Tools](tools.md), and [Connection lifecycle](lifecycle.md) for the provider-agnostic workflows.

### Browser connections

ElevenLabs serves OpenAI's client-secret endpoint, but not its WebRTC one, so
[browser WebRTC](deployment.md#browser-webrtc-server-sideband) isn't available.
[`create_client_secret()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.openai.OpenAIRealtimeModel.create_client_secret] still mints the
short-lived credential ElevenLabs' own browser guide uses: a browser running OpenAI's Realtime SDK passes it as
the API key and opens a WebSocket to `wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/realtime` itself. The secret is bound
to the session your agent configures, but the conversation then runs in the browser, outside Pydantic AI.

### Gateway

Eleven Realtime is not currently available through the [Pydantic AI Gateway](../gateway.md). Connect with an
`elevenlabs:<model>` model string, or with `provider='elevenlabs'` or an `ElevenLabsProvider`.

### Session length

ElevenLabs closes a session once it reaches its maximum duration (600 seconds unless
`elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds` says otherwise). With a [reconnect policy](lifecycle.md#reconnecting), the
session reconnects, and the new session gets the [replayed local history](lifecycle.md#state-restoration), so the
call carries on. Without a reconnect policy, or once its reconnects are used up, the session raises a
[`RealtimeError`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeError] with ElevenLabs' close reason.

ElevenLabs also closes a session that hasn't received anything from the client for 60 seconds, which happens
whenever no microphone audio is streaming, as in a text-only or push-to-talk session. To keep such a session open,
the connection sends an empty audio append (which adds no audio) after 45 seconds without sending anything.

### Provider-specific quirks {#eleven-realtime-quirks}

- ElevenLabs' semantic VAD can report that the user stopped speaking, then hear them carry on in the same turn,
  so [`RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent] and
  [`RealtimeInputSpeechEndEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeInputSpeechEndEvent] can come more than once per
  turn. The turn joins the history once ElevenLabs commits it.
- Eleven Realtime writes expressive audio tags such as `[cheerful]` into its replies to direct the delivery, and
  sends them as part of the transcript. Pydantic AI removes them, from the streamed transcript and the one in history
  alike, and keeps them, in order and without brackets, in the response's `provider_details['audio_tags']`
  (`['cheerful']`). Only lowercase words in square brackets count as tags, so citations (`[1]`), Markdown links, and
  placeholders like `[Your Name]` stay in the text. Set `elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags=False` to keep the transcript
  as ElevenLabs sends it.
- When ElevenLabs replies to something the user said while a tool call is still running, it abandons the call: its
  result never reaches the model, and a response asked for after it never comes. The session then
  gets a recoverable [`RealtimeSessionErrorEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSessionErrorEvent] of type
  `'tool_calls_abandoned'` naming the calls. The tool keeps running and its result is still recorded in history, but
  no reply to it is waited for: [`RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent] and
  [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] come when the response that cut in ends.
- ElevenLabs makes parallel tool calls as back-to-back responses of one call each, and answers all their results
  with one reply, which the session waits for once:
  [`RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent] and
  [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] come when it ends.
- `eleven_realtime_v1_max` sometimes answers a question that needs a tool with two responses: a spoken preamble
  ("Let me check the weather…") that completes on its own, then the tool call in a response nobody asked for.
  Nothing links the two, so [`RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent] and
  [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] can come after the preamble, and the
  tool call and the answer follow as an exchange of their own. History is unaffected. Don't assume the first turn
  completion after such a question carries the answer: keep consuming the session's events.
- The protocol follows OpenAI Realtime, but feature support comes from the ElevenLabs model profile; avoid
  assuming every OpenAI behavior is available.

# Events

Iterating a [`RealtimeSession`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession] yields the session's event
stream: content parts, tool activity, turn boundaries, reconnects, and recoverable errors. The
high-level [`stream_audio()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.stream_audio] and
[`stream_transcripts()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.stream_transcripts] views described in
[Audio, images, and transcripts](audio.md) are derived from this same stream, so most applications
iterate the session for control flow and leave media to the views.

If nothing is iterating the session, the session keeps the most recent 512 part delta events
(audio, transcript, and text) and the most recent 512 structural events for a late `async for`;
older ones are discarded. Discarding a part's start discards the rest of that part with it, so a late
iterator never receives a delta it cannot attach to a part. A failure parked for the consumer is
never discarded.

## Event reference

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| [`PartStartEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.PartStartEvent] | A speech, text, or tool part started. |
| [`PartDeltaEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.PartDeltaEvent] | Incremental speech audio/transcript or text content. |
| [`PartEndEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.PartEndEvent] | A finalized part; retained speech audio appears here, not at part start. |
| [`FunctionToolCallEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.FunctionToolCallEvent] | A local function tool began executing. |
| [`FunctionToolResultEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.FunctionToolResultEvent] | A local function tool produced a result — a return, a failure, or a retry. |
| [`DeferredToolRequestsEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.DeferredToolRequestsEvent] | A tool call was deferred (e.g. needs approval); emitted before any inline capability handler runs. |
| [`DeferredToolResultsEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.DeferredToolResultsEvent] | An inline capability handler resolved the deferred requests; the results go through normal tool processing. |
| [`EnqueuedMessagesEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.EnqueuedMessagesEvent] | Enqueued content was delivered into session history. |
| [`CustomEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.CustomEvent] / [`CapabilityEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.CapabilityEvent] | A tool or capability hook [emitted](capabilities.md#the-event-stream) an application or capability event. |
| [`RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent] | The provider detected that the user started speaking, when the profile declares [`emits_input_speech_events`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeModelProfile.emits_input_speech_events]. |
| [`RealtimeInputSpeechEndEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeInputSpeechEndEvent] | The provider detected the end of user speech, when the profile declares [`emits_input_speech_events`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeModelProfile.emits_input_speech_events]. |
| [`RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent] | The provider reported an interrupted model response. |
| [`RealtimeInputTranscriptionErrorEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeInputTranscriptionErrorEvent] | One user turn could not be transcribed; the session remains usable. |
| [`RealtimeOutputSpeechStartEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeOutputSpeechStartEvent] / [`RealtimeOutputSpeechEndEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeOutputSpeechEndEvent] | The model became, or stopped being, audible. These are emitted on a gpt-realtime or Azure OpenAI [WebRTC sideband](deployment.md#browser-webrtc-server-sideband), where the provider owns audio playback. |
| [`RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent] | The exchange is over: the model gave every reply it owed (or, after a [failure](#the-turn-boundary), never will), and no tool remains active. |
| [`RealtimeSessionReconnectEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSessionReconnectEvent] | The connection was automatically re-established. |
| [`RealtimeSessionErrorEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSessionErrorEvent] | A recoverable provider error occurred; the session remains usable. |

A part's `index` identifies it for the whole session. A provider can finish an output item after a later
item has started, so text of the item's transcript can arrive after its part ended: the session then
streams that part again under the same `index`, and the new
[`PartStartEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.PartStartEvent] replaces the part as it ended. Keep parts by
`index` rather than adding one for every [`PartEndEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.PartEndEvent].

## Shared and realtime-only events

The first nine rows are [`AgentStreamEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.AgentStreamEvent] members from
[`pydantic_ai.messages`][pydantic_ai.messages] — the same events a
[standard streamed run](../agent.md#streaming-all-events) yields, so event-handling code written for
a text agent (rendering parts, logging tool calls) works on a session unchanged. The `Realtime*`
rows are [`RealtimeSessionEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.RealtimeSessionEvent] members, the part of
`AgentStreamEvent` that only a session emits: speech detection, interruption, turn completion,
reconnection, and recoverable errors have no equivalent in a request-response run.

A capability's [event stream hooks](../hooks.md#event-stream-hooks) see both kinds flow through the
same stream; see [Capabilities and hooks](capabilities.md#the-event-stream).

## The turn boundary

Use [`RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent] as the exchange
boundary. A model can speak, call a tool, and speak again, so receiving speech — or a tool result —
does not imply that the turn is done.

The event marks the end of what [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply]
waits for. When a response ends, the session emits it if the model owes nothing more: no reply to anything
sent, no answer to a tool's result, and no response still under way.

Only the response that answers an input settles its reply: a response already under way when the input reached
the provider never saw it, so it doesn't. Text sent while the model is answering therefore usually gets a reply of
its own, and the event comes once that reply ends too. How a provider answers such text varies: GPT-Live speaks to
it in the reply it is giving (see [OpenAI](openai.md#typed-text-runs-the-backend)), and some Gemini Live models
cut their reply off for it (see [Gemini](gemini.md#provider-specific-quirks)).

A response the user cuts off by speaking ends the exchange, as does a response the provider started on its own
(server-side voice activity detection). The user's transcript can still finish after it.

A [tool that raises](tools.md#function-tools) doesn't end the exchange: the model is told the call failed, and the
event comes once it has answered that. An exchange that fails also ends with the event, once: when a tool's result
would pass a [usage limit](../agent.md#usage-limits), or a failed tool's result can't be sent, the model never gets
what it needs to reply. The event follows the exception in the event stream, or comes as the response still under
way ends.

## Reading raw audio events

The audio stream *is* these events under the hood:
[`stream_audio()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.stream_audio] is a bounded view over the
speech part deltas, and most applications should use it. As an advanced alternative, play
[`SpeechPartDelta.audio_chunk`][pydantic_ai.messages.SpeechPartDelta.audio_chunk] from raw
[`PartDeltaEvent`][pydantic_ai.messages.PartDeltaEvent]s. Model audio arrives in full whether or not
history retention is enabled. When output audio is retained, the final
[`SpeechPart`][pydantic_ai.messages.SpeechPart] contains the whole turn again as a WAV snapshot for
[history](history.md#retaining-audio); do not play both or the turn will play twice.

# Google Gemini Live

[`GoogleRealtimeModel`][pydantic_ai.realtime.google.GoogleRealtimeModel] connects an agent to Gemini
Live, including native audio, live images, and provider-native tools. Start with the
[realtime quickstart](overview.md#quickstart) or [camera example](../examples/realtime-camera.md).

## Setup

To use Gemini Live models, install `pydantic-ai-slim` with the `google-realtime` optional group,
which bundles the `google-genai` SDK together with the realtime transport dependencies:

```bash
pip/uv-add "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime]"
```

Authentication comes from `provider`, mirroring
[`GoogleModel`][pydantic_ai.models.google.GoogleModel]. Use `provider='google'` for the Gemini
Developer API or `provider='google-cloud'` for Vertex AI/ADC, with API keys and credentials
configured as described in the [Google model documentation](../models/google.md#configuration).
Pass a [`GoogleProvider`][pydantic_ai.providers.google.GoogleProvider] or
[`GoogleCloudProvider`][pydantic_ai.providers.google_cloud.GoogleCloudProvider] for custom
credentials, project, region, or client.

## Model names

Use a Gemini Live model ID, for example `gemini-3.8-live`, `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`, or
`gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest`. Live models differ in thinking, asynchronous tools, and
output behavior; the profile resolved from the model ID describes what each one supports. Use the
[official Gemini Live documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live) as the canonical
model and availability source.

Vertex AI and the [Pydantic AI Gateway](../gateway.md) use different model IDs and locations from
the Gemini Developer API:

| API | Model ID | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini Developer API | `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest` | n/a (no location) |
| Gemini Developer API | `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` | n/a (no location) |
| Gemini Developer API | `gemini-3.8-live` | n/a (no location) |
| Gemini Developer API | `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking` | n/a (no location) |
| Vertex AI / gateway | `gemini-live-2.5-flash` | `global` |
| Vertex AI / gateway | `gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio` | `us-central1` |

The Developer API IDs are not available on Vertex AI. Configure the matching Vertex location on
[`GoogleCloudProvider`][pydantic_ai.providers.google_cloud.GoogleCloudProvider] or in the gateway;
the gateway example below uses `gemini-live-2.5-flash` and therefore requires `global`.

### Extended thinking

`gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking` reasons in the background while it keeps talking, so it can speak
a filler ("Let me check those flights for you"), run a tool, and answer — all within one exchange. It
differs from every other Live model in three ways the model handles for you:

- **It requires a thinking level.** One is sent even when the session asks for nothing, at the cheapest
  level the model accepts, because reasoning costs latency. Ask for more with
  [`thinking`](../capabilities/thinking.md)`='medium'` or `'high'`. `thinking=False` means "as little as
  possible" here rather than "off", since the model has no off.
- **Its tool calls are always asynchronous.** Its profile's
  [`async_tool_call_mode`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeModelProfile.async_tool_call_mode] is
  `'always'`, since the model has no blocking mode, so an explicit `async_tool_calls=False` is ignored, with an
  [`UnsupportedSettingWarning`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnsupportedSettingWarning] when the session has tools.
- **Its spoken filler doesn't end the turn.** Gemini closes the filler's response and says the
  interaction is still in progress, so the filler and the tool call it was stalling for are recorded
  as one `ModelResponse`, and `RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent` and
  [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] both wait for the model to
  actually finish. A UI that shows "thinking…" should key off those. An utterance the user barges in on is the
  exception: it really is over, and is recorded as its own interrupted response.

`gemini-3.8-live` is the same family without background reasoning. It rejects a thinking *level*, so
the shared [`thinking`](../capabilities/thinking.md) setting is ignored rather than sent. Unlike older
Live models it defaults to asynchronous tool calls, so Pydantic AI declares tools `BLOCKING` unless
`async_tool_calls=True` asks otherwise, keeping the same default as every other model.

Both 3.8 models keep proactive audio permanently on, so there's nothing for `google_proactive_audio`
to turn on and it can be left unset. Gemini rejects an explicit `False`, which Pydantic AI never sends,
and `True` is accepted too. Neither supports affective dialog, and neither does
`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`: `google_affective_dialog=True` raises `UserError` when the session connects.

## Settings

[`GoogleRealtimeModelSettings`][pydantic_ai.realtime.google.GoogleRealtimeModelSettings] — the
realtime counterpart of [model run settings](../agent.md#model-run-settings) — extends the
[shared settings](overview.md#shared-settings) with Google generation and Live controls:

```python
from pydantic_ai.realtime.google import GoogleRealtimeModel, GoogleRealtimeModelSettings

settings = GoogleRealtimeModelSettings(
    temperature=0.7,
    top_p=0.9,
    google_voice='Puck',
    google_language_code='en-US',
    google_affective_dialog=True,
    google_vad={'start_sensitivity': 'high', 'end_sensitivity': 'low'},
    google_turn_coverage='all_video',
    google_context_compression={'trigger_tokens': 16000, 'target_tokens': 8000},
)
model = GoogleRealtimeModel('gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest', settings=settings)
```

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `google_voice`, `google_language_code` | Voice and output language. A Live session speaks in one voice: the deprecated `google_multi_speaker` raises when the session connects |
| `google_affective_dialog` | Emotion-aware delivery, on the 2.5 models (not 3.1 Flash Live or the 3.8 models) |
| `google_proactive_audio` | Model-decided speech on native-audio models, served on the Developer API's `v1alpha` (see below). Always on for the 3.8 models |
| `google_vad` | Exact automatic VAD; fully overrides shared [`turn_detection`](turns.md#automatic-turn-detection) |
| `google_activity_handling`, `google_turn_coverage` | [Interruption](turns.md#barge-in) behavior and which input belongs to a turn |
| `google_input_transcription`, `google_output_transcription` | Native [transcription](audio.md#input-transcription) switches, enabled by default |
| `google_context_compression` | Sliding-window compression for long sessions |
| `google_enable_session_resumption` | Native state restoration; enabled automatically by a `reconnect` policy |
| `google_config_overrides` | Raw `LiveConnectConfig` keys merged last as a forward-compatibility escape hatch |

`google_voice` is the provider voice setting. `google_thinking_config` takes precedence over the
shared [`thinking`](../capabilities/thinking.md) setting when a token budget or other
Gemini-specific control is needed.

Gemini Live has no tool-choice configuration, so it can't force a tool call: a
[`tool_choice`](tools.md#restricting-the-available-tools) of `'required'` or a list of tool names
raises a `UserError` before connecting. To limit the model to some tools, pass
[`ToolOrOutput(function_tools=[...])`][pydantic_ai.settings.ToolOrOutput] instead. It also can't stop
the model from calling several tools at once, so `parallel_tool_calls=False` warns with an
[`UnsupportedSettingWarning`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnsupportedSettingWarning].

!!! note "`google_proactive_audio` dials the `v1alpha` API"
    Gemini serves `proactivity` on the Developer API's `v1alpha` only; on any other version the
    session is closed with `1007 Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "proactivity" at
    'setup'`. When the provider was built from an API key (the default `'google'` provider, or
    `GoogleProvider(api_key=...)`), a session with `google_proactive_audio=True` opens its Live
    connection with a separate `v1alpha` client built from that key, closed when the session ends.
    The provider's own client is left as it is, so ordinary
    [`GoogleModel`][pydantic_ai.models.google.GoogleModel] requests sharing it keep their version.

    A client you built yourself can't be rebuilt that way, so pass one that is already on `v1alpha`;
    connecting with one on another version raises [`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError]:

    ```python {title="proactive_audio.py"}
    from google.genai import Client, types

    from pydantic_ai.providers.google import GoogleProvider
    from pydantic_ai.realtime.google import GoogleRealtimeModel, GoogleRealtimeModelSettings

    client = Client(
        api_key='your-api-key', http_options=types.HttpOptions(api_version='v1alpha')
    )
    model = GoogleRealtimeModel(
        'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest',
        provider=GoogleProvider(client=client),
        settings=GoogleRealtimeModelSettings(google_proactive_audio=True),
    )
    ```

    Unavailable on Vertex AI, whose version line has no `v1alpha`.

!!! warning "Keep automatic VAD enabled"
    Pydantic AI does not expose Gemini activity markers or manual turn verbs. Do not set
    `google_vad={'disabled': True}`; shared `turn_detection=False` is rejected for the same reason.

### Asynchronous tool calls

Gemini normally pauses generation while a function tool is outstanding. On the native-audio models and
`gemini-3.8-live`, set the shared
[`async_tool_calls`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeModelSettings.async_tool_calls] setting to `True` to
let it keep speaking and answering: tools are then declared `NON_BLOCKING`, and their results are
returned with `INTERRUPT` scheduling, so each cuts into whatever the model is saying when it arrives.
This is best for slow tools, since a fast result can cut off speech that barely started. What the model
says while the tool runs is recorded with the call, ahead of its result: see
[Transcription and history edge cases](history.md#transcription-and-history-edge-cases).

The other Live models accept a `NON_BLOCKING` declaration and then wait for the result anyway, so
they ignore the setting, and `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`, which has no blocking mode, runs every
tool call this way regardless — see [Extended thinking](#extended-thinking). The deprecated
`google_async_tool_calls` setting still works as an alias, with a deprecation warning.

### Native tools

Gemini Live maps [`WebSearch`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.WebSearch] to Google Search grounding, the
only native tool it supports — no Live model runs native code execution or URL context, so neither
[`CodeExecutionTool`][pydantic_ai.native_tools.CodeExecutionTool] nor
[`WebFetch`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.WebFetch] is advertised in `supported_native_tools`. Give
those a [`local=` fallback](tools.md#native-tools) and the session runs the local tool instead:
[`NativeOrLocalTool(native=CodeExecutionTool(), local=...)`](../capabilities/overview.md#building-your-own),
or `WebFetch(native=False, local=True)`, which requires the `web-fetch` optional group (`pip/uv-add "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime,web-fetch]"`).
Google Search grounding takes no domain filters or usage limit, so a `WebSearch` with
`allowed_domains`, `blocked_domains`, `max_uses`, or `external_web_access=False` set fails before the session connects (see
[restricting parameters](../native-tools.md#restricting-parameters)).

### Specialist streaming models

Gemini also serves specialist streaming models on the same endpoint. The robotics ones, like
`gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview`, are perception models rather than voice assistants: they take
in a live audio and video stream and answer in text, for a robot's controller to act on, and reject
audio output. Their profile reports
[`supports_audio_output=False`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeModelProfile.supports_audio_output], so a
session on one asks for text by default and records the answers as `TextPart`s:

```python {title="robot_perception.py"}
from pydantic_ai import Agent

perception = Agent(instructions='You are the perception module of a robot.')


async def main(frames=()):
    async with perception.realtime('google:gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview').session() as session:
        for frame in frames:
            await session.send(frame)  # a `BinaryImage` per camera frame
        await session.send('What object is in front of you?')
        await session.wait_for_reply()
```

For a streaming model the built-in profile doesn't describe, correct the facts with
[`profile=`](overview.md#provider-support), which resolves like a
[standard model profile](../models/overview.md#inspecting-a-models-profile).

## Feature support and limitations

| Feature | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audio format | Full feature support | Mono PCM16, 16 kHz input and 24 kHz output |
| Text output | Vertex `gemini-live-2.5-flash` and the [robotics streaming models](#specialist-streaming-models) only | The other Live models reject a `TEXT` response modality, so `output_modality='text'` raises; read the answer from the transcript on the `SpeechPart`. The robotics models only write text, which is their default |
| Image/live video input | Full feature support | [Images](audio.md#images); `google_turn_coverage='all_video'` keeps streamed frames in context |
| Manual turns | Unsupported | [Automatic turn detection](turns.md#automatic-turn-detection) is required |
| Explicit interruption/truncation | Unsupported | Gemini [interrupts server-side](turns.md#barge-in) and emits `RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent` |
| Input transcription | Full feature support | Native [transcription](audio.md#input-transcription), enabled by default; no separate model ID |
| Native tools | Limited parameter support | Google Search grounding only; URL context and code execution fall back to a [`local=` tool](tools.md#native-tools) (see above) |
| Usage | Full feature support | Token and modality breakdowns; function-call usage may arrive on a later turn |
| State-restoring reconnect | Full feature support | Requires [session resumption](#session-resumption) plus a reconnect policy |

See [Audio, images, and transcripts](audio.md), [Turns and interruptions](turns.md),
[Tools](tools.md), and [Connection lifecycle](lifecycle.md) for the provider-agnostic workflows.

## Gateway

To route through the [Pydantic AI Gateway](../gateway.md), use a `gateway/`-prefixed model string:

```python
from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a helpful voice assistant.')
realtime = agent.realtime('gateway/google:gemini-live-2.5-flash')
```

The gateway proxies Gemini Live through the Vertex upstream, so configure a region that supports
the selected model as listed in [Model names](#model-names). `gateway/google-cloud` is an alias. See
[Gateway trace propagation](observability.md#gateway-trace-propagation).

## Session resumption

For [state-restoring reconnects](lifecycle.md#state-restoration), set the `reconnect` setting to a
[`ReconnectPolicy`][pydantic_ai.realtime.ReconnectPolicy]; session resumption is enabled
automatically alongside it (`google_enable_session_resumption` can still request handles without a
policy, and explicitly setting it to `False` next to a policy raises
[`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError] rather than silently losing the conversation).
Reconnection uses the latest in-memory server handle and emits `state_restored=True`, unless the
drop cut off an exchange the resumed session no longer has (see
[State restoration](lifecycle.md#state-restoration)). A drop before the server has issued a handle
dials a fresh session instead and replays the session's local history into it, as on the other
providers.

!!! note "The connection cap can briefly interrupt a turn"
    Gemini sends `GoAway` shortly before its provider-defined connection cap. Pydantic AI reconnects
    after the drop rather than proactively on `GoAway`, so a long call can briefly drop mid-turn.
    This is tracked in [#6643](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues/6643).

## Provider-specific quirks

- What happens to text (or a tool result) that reaches the model while it generates a reply depends on the model:
  - The native-audio models finish the reply, and answer the text in a turn after it.
  - `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`, `gemini-3.8-live`, and Vertex's `gemini-live-2.5-flash` cut the reply off: they
    emit `RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent`, the partial reply is recorded as interrupted, and the next turn answers
    the text. `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` also cancels the tool calls the cut-off turn was waiting on, and makes
    them again.

  [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] and
  [`RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent`](events.md#the-turn-boundary) wait for the reply to the text. Where the text went out
  just as a reply began, before the session saw it start, telling which reply answers the text takes the
  `google_input_cuts_off_reply` profile flag: the cut-off reply then answers only what started it. It is on for
  `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` and `gemini-3.8-live`, which report where in the audio the user started speaking,
  telling a reply the user spoke over apart from one text cut off. It is off for Vertex's `gemini-live-2.5-flash`,
  which reports no speech, and for the native-audio models, so there a wait for such text can end with the reply
  already under way. For a model not covered (`gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`, say) that cuts its reply off
  this way and reports speech, turn the flag on with `profile=`.
- Gemini reports response interruption but not user speech-start/end events, so local playback is
  flushed on `RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent`, and Gemini sessions record no `user speech` span (see
  [Logfire instrumentation](observability.md#logfire-instrumentation)).
- When Gemini says why it ended a turn, the response records it the way a
  [`GoogleModel`][pydantic_ai.models.google.GoogleModel] response does: a malformed function call is
  `finish_reason='error'`, refused input or unsafe output is `'content_filter'`, and the raw reason
  (such as `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`) is kept in `provider_details['finish_reason']`.
- `send()` sends an [image](audio.md#images) as a live video frame. Spoken turns see video frames,
  but typed turns don't on the Live models. So a typed turn (`send('...')`) also carries the most
  recent image sent in the last 10 seconds in its own content, ahead of the text. That image is sent,
  and counted as input, twice. Context text (`respond=False`) and audio don't carry it. To ask about an
  image in writing, send the two together so the question is always inside the window:
  `session.send([image, 'What is this?'])`. The `google_text_turns_see_video_frames` profile flag
  controls the second send.
- Gemini 3.x Live models transcribe the user's speech even with input transcription
  [turned off](audio.md#input-transcription). Pydantic AI discards those transcripts, so the setting
  still keeps the user's words out of history, but they are still produced on Google's side.
- After resuming from a handle it issued at the start of a turn, `gemini-3.8-live` can stream that
  turn's answer without ever sending `turn_complete`, then answer the next input with
  `RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent` and nothing more. The reply stays open, so
  [`wait_for_reply()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession.wait_for_reply] doesn't return. This
  happens on Google's side, and no client-side workaround is known.
- Native transcription can produce only a completed sentence on some models.
  [Caption UIs](audio.md#live-captions) should replace text from `TranscriptUpdate.transcript`
  rather than assume incremental deltas.
